briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
A complex and contradictory de-escalation attempt in Lebanon is underway, with US President Trump announcing a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, which both sides reportedly accepted after intense cross-border attacks and significant Israeli casualties. This development occurred amidst heightened Iranian military actions against US assets and strong threats to close the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iran to halt talks with the US.

IRAN
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy reportedly targeted the US-Israeli-linked vessel "MSC Sariska" with a cruise missile in Iraqi waters, retaliating for a US attack on the Iranian vessel "Lian Star" in the Oman Sea. The IRGC also claimed responsibility for a ballistic missile attack on a US base in Kuwait, which the US Central Command confirmed were intercepted. In response to Iran downing a US MQ-1 drone, the US Central Command conducted "defensive strikes" on Iranian radar and command and control sites in Goruk, Iran, and Qeshm Island over the weekend, with satellite images reportedly showing damage to at least 20 US military sites. Internally, three explosions were reported in Bandar Abbas, and two IRGC members were killed in Qom due to an explosion of "remaining ammunition from the war with Israel and the US." Iran executed two protesters, Mehrdad Mohammadi-nia and Ashkan Maleki, in Tehran for charges including mosque burning and blocking streets. Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf warned of halting negotiations if "crimes" continue, and Quds Force Commander Qaani threatened to activate other fronts and "mirror Bab al-Mandab Strait traffic conditions with the Strait of Hormuz" if Israeli aggression in Gaza and Lebanon persists. Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi reiterated that any ceasefire with the US must cover all fronts, including Lebanon, and Iran halted indirect message exchanges with the US in protest of Israeli actions in Lebanon and Gaza.

ISRAEL
Israel experienced significant military and civilian developments. Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester (30), a doctor with the Givati Brigade, was killed in an explosive drone attack in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, southern Lebanon, which also wounded seven other troops, including two seriously. Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati (20) of the Maglan Unit was killed in a separate Hezbollah explosive drone attack in Yohmor, southern Lebanon, near Beaufort Castle, with three other soldiers wounded. The IDF announced the killing of Mohammed Mousa Mteirek, a Hezbollah missile unit commander, in an airstrike in Nabatieh and also eliminated three Hezbollah operatives north of the Litani River who were preparing drone launches. The IDF also destroyed a Hezbollah launcher that targeted Tiberias and withdrew the 146th Division from southern Lebanon after three months of operations. PM Netanyahu stated Israel's intention to strike Hezbollah targets in Beirut's Dahiyeh if attacks on Israeli cities continue, though reports indicated these strikes were delayed or cancelled following US intervention. Home front areas, including Shlomi, Rosh Hanikra, Kiryat Shmona, Safed, and Karmiel, experienced numerous rocket and drone sirens. The Knesset approved a bill for its dissolution in a first reading and again rejected Finance Minister Smotrich's VAT exemption order. Thousands of Haredi protesters blocked major roads and railway lines, including Highway 4 and the Jerusalem railway, in protest of the conscription law. The High Court of Justice approved the appointment of Maj. Gen. Roman Gofman as the next Mossad chief. France banned Israel from presenting at the Eurosatory arms exhibition in Paris.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, the IDF killed Jamal Abu Aoun, a Hamas platoon commander and doctor at Yafa Hospital in Deir al-Balah, stating he was involved in advancing attacks and rearmament efforts in violation of the ceasefire. New Israeli evacuation orders reportedly forced Gaza City families from their homes. In the West Bank, IDF forces operated in Hebron, raiding the home of a terrorist who carried out a ramming attack at Gush Junction, which injured three Israeli civilians.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued intense operations, launching multiple rockets and explosive drones at northern Israel. These attacks triggered numerous sirens across communities like Shlomi, Rosh Hanikra, Metula, Kiryat Shmona, Safed, and Karmiel. Explosive FPV drones killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded ten others in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Yohmor. Hezbollah also claimed to have disabled two armored vehicles and targeted a Merkava tank in Hadatha. Israel responded with airstrikes, killing Hezbollah missile commander Mohammed Mousa Mteirek in Nabatieh and three operatives north of the Litani River. Israeli strikes also hit Al-Marwaniyah and Jabal Amel Hospital in Tyre, reportedly killing 4 civilians and injuring 20. The IDF issued evacuation warnings to residents of Beirut's Dahiyeh district, stating it would strike terror targets there if Hezbollah attacks continue. This threat was reportedly followed by a US-brokered ceasefire announcement from President Trump, stating both Israel and Hezbollah agreed to cease fire, though Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's subsequent statements indicated Israel's intent to continue operations in southern Lebanon and reserve the right to strike Beirut. Ministers from Germany and Norway cancelled their visit to Beirut due to security risks.

SYRIA & IRAQ
A commercial vessel was attacked twice in the Persian Gulf, approximately 40 nautical miles southeast of Umm Qasr, Iraq, causing a fire. The IRGC Navy claimed responsibility for targeting the "MSC Sariska" in Iraqi waters in retaliation for a US attack on an Iranian vessel. The Iraqi group "Ashab al-Kahf" declared readiness to make Eilat a "zone of operations" if Beirut's Dahiyeh is attacked. US Central Command conducted defensive strikes on Iranian radar and command and control sites in Goruk, Iran, and Qeshm Island over the weekend, following Iran's downing of a US MQ-1 drone.

GULF STATES
Qatar played a diplomatic role, with Qatari officials mediating to establish a ceasefire in Lebanon and contacting the US for de-escalation. Washington reportedly informed Qatar that planned Dahiyeh attacks were cancelled after the Trump-Netanyahu call. The Qatari Foreign Minister discussed regional developments and maritime security with his Iranian counterpart, affirming support for a comprehensive agreement. Kuwait's military activated its air defense systems in response to two ballistic missiles launched from Iran towards a US base in Kuwait, which were intercepted by US forces. Al-Sharq Al-Saudi reported that Hezbollah accepted the US proposal for a mutual cessation of hostilities, conditional on Beirut's Dahiyeh not being targeted.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Alleged Lebanon Ceasefire:** US President Trump announced a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, stating that Israeli forces en route to Beirut were turned back, and both sides agreed to cease fire. This followed Israeli threats to strike Beirut's Dahiyeh and Iranian warnings.
2.  **Israeli Casualties in Lebanon:** Two Israeli soldiers, Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester (30) and Staff Sgt. Adam Tzarfati (20), were killed in separate Hezbollah explosive drone attacks in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah and Yohmor, southern Lebanon, on June 1. A total of 10 other soldiers were wounded in these attacks.
3.  **Iran Suspends Talks with US:** Iran halted indirect message exchanges with the US via mediators in protest of Israeli military operations in Lebanon and Gaza, with reports suggesting consideration of a Strait of Hormuz blockade and activating other fronts like Bab al-Mandab.
4.  **Iranian Retaliatory Strikes:** The IRGC Navy claimed responsibility for targeting the "US-Israeli-linked vessel MSC Sariska" with a cruise missile in Iraqi waters, and attacked a US base in Kuwait with ballistic missiles, which were intercepted.
5.  **US Strikes in Iran:** US Central Command conducted "defensive strikes" on Iranian radar and command and control sites in Goruk, Iran, and Qeshm Island over the weekend in response to Iran downing a US MQ-1 drone.
6.  **Hezbollah Missile Commander Killed:** IDF announced the killing of Mohammed Mousa Mteirek, a Hezbollah missile array unit commander responsible for hundreds of rocket and drone launches, in an Israeli Air Force strike in Nabatieh yesterday.
7.  **New Mossad Chief Approved:** The Israeli High Court of Justice approved the appointment of Major General Roman Gofman as the next head of the Mossad, rejecting petitions against his nomination.
8.  **Haredi Protests:** Thousands of Haredi protesters blocked major roads and railway lines in Israel, including Highway 4 and the Jerusalem railway, protesting the new conscription law and detention of draft evaders.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation remains high despite a US-brokered de-escalation effort in Lebanon, due to conflicting statements on the extent of the ceasefire and Israel's continued operations in southern Lebanon. Iran's decision to suspend talks with the US and its explicit threats to maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Bab al-Mandab) and to activate new fronts signal a critical red line for Tehran, risking a broader regional conflict. Active flashpoints include the Israel-Lebanon border, the Persian Gulf/Strait of Hormuz with ongoing naval engagements, and potential renewed hostilities in Gaza. Military postures are heightened, with Iran declaring "100% readiness" and Israel maintaining significant forces in southern Lebanon, while adjusting its divisional deployments.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
US President Trump announced a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, claiming personal intervention with both sides, but also stated a willingness to continue a "steel-like" blockade against Iran and that he "doesn't care" if talks with Iran are over. US Central Command continued "defensive strikes" in Iran. Qatar actively mediated the Lebanon de-escalation and supported a comprehensive agreement. Kuwait responded to Iranian missile launches by activating its air defense. Within the EU, ambassadors are set to discuss sanctions against Israeli ministers, while France banned Israel from a major arms exhibition. German Chancellor Merz is planning a meeting to soften relations with Trump ahead of the NATO summit. Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister claimed US failure against Iran, and its UN envoy accused Israel of expanding occupation in Lebanon, linking regional deterioration to US-Israeli aggression and stressing the impact on Iran-US negotiations. The UN expressed "deep concern" about Lebanon and called for a ceasefire.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the alleged Lebanon ceasefire: Trump declared a complete cessation of hostilities, but Netanyahu affirmed Israel's intent to strike Dahiyeh if attacks continue and to proceed with planned operations in southern Lebanon. Israeli political figures widely criticized Netanyahu's perceived capitulation. The status of US-Iran talks is also ambiguous, with Trump initially stating rapid progress, while Iran announced suspension due to Israeli actions in Lebanon, prompting Trump to claim ignorance and indifference. Propaganda indicators are visible in the framing of events by Iranian media (e.g., Israeli actions as "crimes"), and by omid dana, who frequently employs highly opinionated and speculative commentary. An unverified report from Axios/Faytuks Network claiming Trump berated Netanyahu for being "crazy" could be a tool for political leverage. Reporting gaps exist concerning the precise terms of the Lebanon de-escalation, the nature of the US "blockade" against Iran, and a clear connection between Michael Tyokin's death and the Lebanon conflict across all sources.
